note: The smaller crowns as city-states (v2 step 5). Each has a type, and its suzerain gains that type's `bonus` every month. Great powers spend renown on envoys (`envoyCost`); a power with at least `sealMin` envoys at a court and more than any rival there has the right to seal suzerainty, by one of three routes: protection (the crown is at war or an enemy army stands on its land), pressure (it fears us: our companies number `pressure.ratio` times its own, and a gift of `pressure.gift` crowns), or peace terms (we hold its capital: the war ends and the capital is returned). A suzerain's armies may cross its vassal's land, and the vassal joins its suzerain's wars. A rival with `courtAway` more envoys than the suzerain courts the vassal away. A suzerain whose Authority falls below `rebel.below` may see a vassal rebel (`rebel.chance` a month): it goes to war, and when its capital is taken the suzerain judges it. Each court asks a favour (`quests`) now and then; the first power to do it gains `questEnvoys` envoys there. Having any envoy at a court opens its borders to that power's armies.

gift.text: asks for {n} crowns to mend its walls

garrison.text: asks for an army at {place} for a month, against brigands

depose.name: Depose the king
depose.text: A new king, our creature, on the old throne.

annex.name: Annex the crown
annex.text: Its lands become ours, sullen and unsettled.

pardon.name: Pardon him
pardon.text: Mercy, and a king who owes us his head.

execute.name: Execute him
execute.text: A head on the gate, and a lesson to every small crown.
